newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's C.Heights seeks to boost rental income.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's C.Heights seeks to boost rental income.

text.p: Malaysian property group Country Heights Holdings Bhd, faced with a dwindling land bank and prospects of slowing growth, is looking to increase its rental income to 50 percent of net earnings.

"We want to see the percentage of recurring income growing to around 50 percent of earnings over the next five years," Country Heights chief executive Michael Yam told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.
Currently, recurring income from rentals of properties and other activities accounted for 10 percent of net profits, he said.
"Whatever we develop, we want to retain at least 10 percent of it (for rental)," said Yam.

Country Heights pioneered the concept of selling subdivided plots of land banks to consumers in Malaysia around 10 years ago. The group's rapid growth has depended heavily on increasing acquisitions of land in prime locations.
Analysts have also described its developments as among Malaysia's most flamboyant properties.

Country Heights' more colourful activities include the Mines Wonderland theme park, a Disney-style recreational facility. This is currently being expanded into a 946-acre (383-hectare) development known as Mines Resort City at a cost of 1.2 billion ringgit ($476 million).

Its pre-tax profit for the six months ended August 31, 1996, rose 71 percent year-on-year to 63 million ringgit. Net profit jumped 61 percent to 42 million ringgit and turnover doubled to 152 million ringgit in the same period.
But to maintain this pace, the group must either acquire new land banks or drive up rental income, analysts said.
Country Heights owns 6,451 acres, according to its 1996 annual report.
"We are constantly looking for new land," said Yam. "But we will only buy land on our terms. If the proposal from the vendor is right, we will immediately write out a cheque," he added.
When asked when Country Heights would announce its next land acquisition, Yam said: "Probably before the end of the next financial year. It will be something big." He gave no further details.

The group's flagship residential development, called Country Heights, on the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur, boasts Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad as one of its clients. It is next to the North-South Expressway, giving residents rapid access to Kuala Lumpur's city centre.
In addition, the group has been diversifying its earnings base by developing leisure and recreational facilities, also giving the group a much needed source of recurring income.

The Mines Resort City will include the Mines Resort and Golf Club which will host the 1999 Golf World Cup. The site will also include the Palace of the Golden Horses Hotel, which Yam described as "six-star plus".
Another project on the same site will be a shopping mall with a canal running through its centre.
All these projects are expected to be completed by the end of 1997.
